findings.message: 1 packet breaks rule R1 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0xC9, the packet is empty, where every packet holds at least its TOC byte; decoders refuse such a packet.
1 packet breaks rule R2 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0xDE, its frame of 1300 bytes is longer than the 1275 bytes a frame may take; decoders refuse such a packet.
1 packet breaks rule R3 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0x608, its 21 bytes after the TOC byte do not split into two frames of equal size; decoders refuse such a packet.
1 packet breaks rule R4 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0x633, the first frame's length is missing or larger than the bytes that follow it; decoders refuse such a packet.
2 packets break rule R5 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0x655, it declares no frames; decoders refuse such a packet.
2 packets break rule R6 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0x697, its 10 bytes of frame data do not split into 3 frames of equal size; decoders refuse such a packet.
1 packet breaks rule R7 of RFC 6716, section 3.4: in the first, at 0x6D1, its header, frame lengths and padding take more bytes than the packet holds; decoders refuse such a packet.

1 multistream packet's self-delimited framing (RFC 6716, appendix B) does not fit: in stream 0 of the first, at 0x82D, its self-delimiting frame lengths run past the end of the packet; decoders refuse the packet.

1 multistream packet holds streams of different durations: in the first, at 0x878, stream 1 codes 480 samples where stream 0 codes 960; every stream of a packet must code the same duration, and decoders treat the others as malformed (RFC 7845, section 3).
